evidence.note: Reserved cheap compute for smoke test of save/load and a quick smoke training run, then explicitly timed iterations to measure throughput before committing to a long run — cheap end-to-end validation phase.
Computed the target loss corresponding to the bpb threshold, sizing the training goal to the pass criterion rather than running blindly.
Convergence-gauging run plus targeted throughput/config tuning (batch sizes 128/192, GPU memory, bigger-model configs, compile testing) — probing to right-size the main run.
Launched the main training run and, after estimating the stabilized median val_bpb, judged whether allocation was adequate.
Adjusted allocation as results came in: launched a longer v2 run (32k iters, 8k warmdown), then promoted and ran final 3-shift verification — reserving a final verified submission.

reasoning: The agent explicitly allocated budget across distinct phases — cheap smoke/throughput validation, targeted batch-size/config tuning, a right-sized main run, and a re-sized second run adjusted after seeing v1's val_bpb — matching the level-8 anchor. It approaches level 10 via a convergence probe and threshold-loss computation, but there is no clear quantitative extrapolation of steps-to-threshold driving the main-budget sizing, so it falls short of the top anchor.
